title: Multi-country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak Situation Report No. 25 (26 October – 1 November 2026) - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: The outbreak situation report was published on 6 November 2026, covering the period from 26 October to 1 November 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is primarily in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria. Ituri is the epicentre, and the affected population includes communities and health facilities in these regions.
analysis.event: A multi-country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (BVD) outbreak remained active, with sustained transmission in the DRC and imported cases requiring continued surveillance and response in Kenya and Nigeria. The report is an official situation report by IOM.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 31 October 2026, the DRC reported 10,467 confirmed cases and 5,103 deaths. In Kenya, nine confirmed cases and two deaths were reported, with seven patients still in treatment. In Nigeria, one confirmed case was under active follow-up, and no contacts tested positive. The report highlights significant gaps in early detection and response capacity.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Disease surveillance and screening continued at points of entry and in health facilities and communities. In Kenya, 20 contacts completed the 21-day monitoring period, while 98 remained under monitoring. In Nigeria, 62 contacts linked to the index case were identified and under follow-up. The situation remains under investigation, with no confirmed cases in Nigeria beyond the single imported case.

analysis.brief_en: The Multi-country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak Situation Report No. 25, published on 6 November 2026, details the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria. As of 31 October 2026, the DRC reported 10,467 confirmed cases and 5,103 deaths, with Ituri being the epicentre accounting for 71% of cases. Kenya had nine confirmed cases and two deaths, with seven patients still in treatment, while Nigeria had one confirmed case under active follow-up. The report emphasizes the need for improved early detection and community-based surveillance, noting that no contacts tested positive in Nigeria. Disease surveillance and screening continued at points of entry and in health facilities, supported by IOM and other partners. The outbreak remains under investigation, with no confirmed cases beyond the single imported one in Nigeria.

analysis.event: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues at a high, sustained level of transmission. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 7 November 2026, the cumulative total of confirmed cases is 10,920, including 5,323 confirmed deaths (CFR 48.7%). In Nigeria, no secondary case has been identified, and contact monitoring is expected to end on 13 November.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Insecurity in Beni health zone in North Kivu and Bafwasende in Tshopo, along with health-worker strikes in Bas-Uélé and Tshopo, and the continued suspension of response activities in Bafwasende, constrain surveillance and response operations. Contact follow-up fell to its lowest level in weeks at the end of the period.

analysis.time: 15 October 2026, with activities between July and September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Eastern Mediterranean Region, specifically Djibouti, Somalia, and Sudan, with vulnerable populations in conflict-affected areas.
analysis.event: WHO is scaling up readiness for Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, following outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and an imported BVD case in Nairobi, Kenya. No confirmed cases in the region yet, but preparations are underway.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No confirmed cases, but potential risk due to conflict, displacement, and overstretched health systems. Additional support is needed for isolation centres, laboratory capacity, and personal protective equipment.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO has deployed multidisciplinary missions, provided diagnostic kits, and supported training and technical assistance. Efforts are ongoing to strengthen laboratory testing, frontline response capacity, and community engagement. Challenges include conflict, insecurity, and restricted access, particularly in countries with major humanitarian emergencies.

analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) is enhancing readiness for Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, focusing on Djibouti, Somalia, and Sudan. This follows outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, as well as an imported BVD case in Nairobi, Kenya. Although no confirmed BVD cases have been reported in the region, WHO has deployed missions to assess national preparedness and identify challenges in surveillance, laboratory capacity, and emergency coordination. Over 150 health workers have been trained in case detection, infection prevention, and control, and more than 70 participants took part in a simulation exercise to test emergency procedures. WHO has also provided diagnostic kits, medical supplies, and US$200,000 from its Contingency Fund for Emergencies. Despite progress, gaps remain in early detection, laboratory confirmation, and resource availability, particularly in conflict-affected areas. WHO continues to work with national authorities and partners to ensure rapid detection, investigation, and management of suspected BVD cases.

analysis.brief_en: A British aid worker diagnosed with Ebola has been medically evacuated to the UK for specialist treatment, as reported by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The individual was transported via a medevac flight with full personal protective equipment (PPE) and is now in a High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) unit at the Royal Free Hospital in London. The UK has well-established systems for managing such cases, including rapid testing and strict infection control protocols. The risk to the UK public remains low, and the spread of Ebola during the transfer is considered extremely unlikely. The patient is being treated in isolation, minimizing the chance of transmission. The UKHSA emphasized that the overall risk to the public has not changed, and healthcare workers involved in treating the patient follow strict protocols to ensure safety. The incident highlights the UK's commitment to supporting humanitarian workers and managing high-consequence infectious diseases.

The 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak tested the assumption that cross-protection from Zaire-based countermeasures would work against other species. It calls for a broader framework, including conserved pan-ebolavirus targets for diagnostics, multivalent vaccine designs, and simulation-based training to improve operational readiness. The response to these challenges requires genomic surveillance and a shift from reactive to continuous monitoring to ensure effective countermeasures can be developed and deployed quickly.

analysis.event: The WHO has approved two new Bundibugyo virus vaccine candidates, ChAdOx1 BDBV and mRNA-1469, for Phase 2/3 clinical trials. This decision follows a review of preclinical and Phase 1 clinical data, which showed very positive results in animal and non-human primate studies.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The Bundibugyo virus has caused over 10,500 confirmed cases and more than 5,300 deaths in the DRC. analysis.brief_en: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) provided an update on the status of Ebola in Nigeria, noting that 28 contacts remain under active surveillance. This follows the confirmation of an imported infection of the Bundibugyo virus from Uganda, with no additional cases reported 21 days later. The NCDC emphasized that being identified as a contact does not equate to having Ebola, and that monitoring helps in early detection and response. The Director-General, Dr. Jide Idris, highlighted ongoing efforts in contact tracing, laboratory testing, and surveillance, urging healthcare workers to remain vigilant and report suspected cases promptly. Additionally, the NCDC addressed other health concerns such as dengue fever, Chikungunya, diphtheria, and Lassa fever, emphasizing the need for public awareness and preparedness. The agency also advised households to eliminate stagnant water, cover food containers, and protect against mosquito and rodent bites. Overall, the response remains active, with teams deployed to support affected states and prevent avoidable deaths.
